title: Tibber - Energy - Large negative consumption around midnight
body:
### The problem

After updating to HA 2021.12.0 late last night, my Energy dashboard shows large negative consumption around midnight for all my meters observed (I have no energy production, so this is clearly wrong). This happened both on a Supervised installation and on an OS installation of HA.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2021.12.0

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

2021.11.5

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Supervised

### Integration causing the issue

Energy

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://<redacted-host>/docs/energy/

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
Not applicable
```


### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
Not that I can see
```


### Additional information

_No response_

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
> If You use sensor.last_meter_consumption_xxx everything seems to work fine.

Yes, but I’m hestitant to do that. The reasoning is like this:

If you look at my snips, you will see that my two meters have the negative consumption on different times. One apparently just before midnight and the other just after midnight. This indicates to me that the resetting of the «accumulated consumption» sensor is not accurately synchronised with midnight.

The `sensor.last_meter_consumption_xxx` sensor updates once an hour (in my case, at least). Whether it updates just before or just after the hour is uncertain and probably a bit random. This means that you either get the accumulation of consumption on the correct hours - or one hour delayed. If it’s one hour delayed, the cost accumulation will be wrong because the energy consumption is multiplied with the price for the incorrect hour.

So probably, what I will do - unless @participant5 has better suggestions - is to create a new sensor which is the [Riemann sum integration](https://<redacted-host>/integrations/integration/) of `sensor.power_xxx`. The Riemann sum integration will accumulate without bounds (until it hits the `float` limit, I presume) and since it does not reset at any time, it will be better suited, I guess, for the Energy component.

```
  - platform: integration
    source: sensor.power_xxx
    name: Energy consumption xxx
    unit_prefix: k
    unit_time: h
    method: left
```

comments.author: participant7
comments.body:
@participant5 When I read [](https://github.com/home-assistant/developers.home-assistant/blob/master/blog/2021-09-20-state_class_total.md) it looks like the total_increasing is indeed correct for this meter.

`For sensors with state_class total_increasing, a decreasing value is interpreted as the start of a new meter cycle or the replacement of the meter.`

This is an accurate representation of the Tibber accumulated_consumption, it's reset once per day. So either, the way this is outputted from Tibber needs to be changed, or the type needs to be changed back to total_increasing.

Your change #60501 says 

"Replace STATE_CLASS_TOTAL_INCREASING with STATE_CLASS_TOTAL for not strictly increasing accumulated consumption/production" 

but when I read the docs it's the other way around, STATE_CLASS_TOTAL_INCREASING was the correct state_class from the beginning?

So STATE_CLASS_TOTAL_INCREASING is not correct

comments.author: participant7
comments.body:
> The sensor is not always increasing: #60490 So STATE_CLASS_TOTAL_INCREASING is not correct

It's more correct than STATE_CLASS_TOTAL since it's reset once per day. TOTAL_INCREASING has logic for handling "meter periods" and resets, which STATE_CLASS_TOTAL doesn't have.

You addressed a diagnostic warning message report by breaking the Energy reporting for all Tibber users. Either this needs a wider fix in how the Tibber/Energy integration is handled, or this change needs to be reverted.

comments.author: participant7
comments.body:
"total, the state represents a total amount that can both increase and decrease, e.g. a net energy meter. When supported, the accumulated growth or decline of the sensor's value since it was first added is updated periodically."

The Tibber integration has both production and consumtion, as two different meters. By this change, you turned the "accumulated" into a net energy meter, that resets once per day. TOTAL_INCREASING might not be perfect for this, but TOTAL is worse. TOTAL_INCREASING logs an warning but otherwise works, TOTAL just makes it report completely wrong values over time because of the daily reset.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: @participant8 Could you give a couple of pointers on how to correct the db? I have a few months worth of Energy consumption stats that are now quite what they used to be (due to the last few days' negative consumptions...)

comments.author: participant8
comments.body: I guess it's slightly off topic in here but in short, get some sqlite editor (the sqlite web addon is fine), find the metadata_id from the statistics_meta table which is for the sensor you want to correct (mine was among the first ones), `select * from statistics_short_term where metadata_id = <the id you found> order by start desc` and find the id in `statistics_short_term` where it started to go backwards, pick the ID before that. Then update by issuing `update statistics_short_term set sum = sum + <the negative part, probably yesterday's consumption> where metadata_id = <the id again> and id > <the first id that jumped backwards>` and repeat for each day. And then do the same for the `statistics` table. And roll back to 2021.11.5 if you can to prevent having to do this every day.. And..do a backup before the updates.. :)
